description: A one-on-one interview of a candidate or official by a local reporter: the reporter's questions and follow-ups, and the answers, commitments, defenses of a record and deflections. Every part is a whole sentence said in public-domain federal records (hearings, the Congressional Record, FEC and EAC meetings, federal oral histories), with record words as slots. A sentence that claims something about the speaker's life or the place names the record fact it needs (requiresFacts); the engine says it only when that fact is in the record.

slots.office: The office, from the office records.
slots.issue: What the question is about, from the topic or measure record.
slots.place: The town or state, from the place records.
slots.bill: A measure the official voted on, from the vote record.
slots.opponent: The other candidate, by name, from the contest record.
slots.claim: What the opponent said, from the statement record.
slots.goal: What the official wants done, from their recorded stance.
slots.topic: A matter the official won't discuss, from the records.
slots.experience: What happened to the official's family, from their own records.

mining.rule: A shape is kept when at least 2 documents say it as a whole sentence and one of them is a public-domain record from 2015 or later, which is its source.
